methodology:
SLC Agrícola operates 26 production units across 8 Brazilian states, with planted area expanding to ~830,000 hectares for the 2025/26 season. Total owned land base (per company website): ~700,000 hectares (~1.73M acres). The model is part-owned, part-leased — only the owned portion is reflected in the property table.

The 10-K equivalent disclosures (SLC files in Brazil; English filings via 6-K) are less granular than US REIT Schedule III. Three production units publicly named with hectares (Pamplona / Goiás 18,637 ha, Pioneira / Maranhão 20,088 ha, Paiaguás / Mato Grosso 54,847 ha) — these are shown individually. The remaining ~23 units are aggregated by region cluster.

Brazilian Cerrado farmland is the most-traded large-scale cropland market in Latin America. 2024-2025 broker comps consistently show:
- Western Bahia (LEM region, top-quality): R$8,500-10,000/acre
- Goiás Class-A: R$7,500-9,000/acre
- Mato Grosso Class-A cotton-soy: R$6,500-8,500/acre
- Matopiba expansion frontier (MA / PI / TO): R$5,500-7,500/acre

SLC's own internally-disclosed land bank value (capital markets day 2024) approximates R$15B for 700K hectares = R$8,650/acre weighted — used as a portfolio-level reality check.

Like BrasilAgro, SLC carries land at cost on the GAAP balance sheet (Brazilian GAAP). The R$4.5B bookLandMM in the comp set is a rough estimate carved from total Net PP&E + biological assets. The FMV-vs-book gap is structurally large because of the cost-vs-fair-value accounting difference.
